name: TPSM53602RDAR
title: TPSM53602: 36 V in, 2 A step-down power module, 1 V to 7 V out, in a 5 mm × 5.5 mm × 4 mm QFN
summary: A complete synchronous buck converter in a 15-pin over-molded QFN: controller, power MOSFETs and a shielded 2.2 µH inductor inside, with input and output capacitors and two feedback resistors outside. It runs from 3.8 V to 36 V and delivers 1 V to 7 V at up to 2 A, switching at 1.4 MHz in PWM and moving to PFM at light load. It has a precision enable that can set a higher UVLO, a power-good flag, a 4 ms soft start, pre-bias start-up, hiccup short-circuit protection and thermal shutdown. Ambient range is -40 °C to 105 °C; it meets CISPR 11 Class B radiated emissions and is pin compatible with the 3 A TPSM53603 and 4 A TPSM53604.
key_figures: 0.985 V min, 1 V typ, 1.015 V max
91% typ at 2 A, 12 V in, 3.3 V out; up to 95%
up to 14 W at 85°C, no airflow

notes: Pin-compatible family members: TPSM53603 (3 A) and TPSM53604 (4 A).

pins.name: VIN
pins.function: Input supply. The input capacitors go from these pins to PGND, placed right at the module.

pins.name: EN
pins.function: Enable. High runs the converter, low stops it. It may be tied straight to VIN and must not be left floating; a two-resistor divider from VIN sets a higher input undervoltage lockout.

pins.name: NC
pins.function: Not tied to anything inside the module. Joining them to the board PGND plane improves shielding and heat flow.

pins.name: DNC
pins.function: Wired to internal circuits. Each goes on its own isolated pad, joined to nothing: not to ground, not to each other, not to any voltage.

pins.name: PGOOD
pins.function: Open-drain power-good flag, pulled low while the feedback voltage is outside its window. Needs a 10-kΩ to 100-kΩ pullup to V5V or to another DC rail below 22 V. Unused, it can be left open or tied to PGND.

pins.name: VOUT
pins.function: Output, from the internal inductor; the load and the output capacitors (to PGND) connect to these pins.

pins.name: FB
pins.function: Feedback. Takes the tap of the output divider: RFBT from the regulation point on VOUT, RFBB down to AGND.

pins.name: AGND
pins.function: Analog ground and the zero reference for the internal references and logic; all electrical figures are given against it. Joined to PGND at one point only.

pins.name: V5V
pins.function: Output of the internal 5-V LDO that runs the control circuits. Not for external loads; it may serve as the pullup supply for PGOOD.

pins.name: PGND
pins.function: Power ground, the thermal pad, carrying the power stage return current. Joined to the supply and load returns and to the VIN and VOUT capacitors.

circuits.title: Simplified schematic
circuits.description: The fewest parts the module needs: a ceramic input capacitor across VIN and ground, EN tied to VIN so it starts as soon as the input is in range, a two-resistor divider from VOUT to FB to AGND setting the output, and the output capacitor. PGND and AGND meet at one point. PGOOD and V5V are unused.

circuits.title: Typical schematic, 24 V to 5 V at 2 A
circuits.description: A 24 V input stepped down to 5 V. Two 10 µF, 50 V ceramics bypass VIN. A 100 kΩ resistor from VIN holds EN high, and the EN node also runs out to an external control line. The 10 kΩ / 2.49 kΩ divider puts 1 V on FB at 5 V out (10 / (5 − 1) = 2.5 kΩ, nearest standard 2.49 kΩ). Two 47 µF, 10 V ceramics sit on the output. PGOOD is pulled up to the module’s own V5V through 100 kΩ. PGND and AGND are joined at one point.
notes: RFBB (2.49 kΩ) returns to AGND and the capacitors to PGND; AGND and PGND are one net, joined at a single point.

circuits.title: Adjustable UVLO
circuits.description: A divider from VIN to EN to AGND raises the input voltage at which the module starts. EN switching starts at 1.23 V typical with 100 mV typical hysteresis; with RENT = 100 kΩ, the RENB values of the UVLO resistor table give start-up thresholds from 6.5 V to 30 V.

operation.text: A synchronous buck converter for 3.8 V to 36 V in and 1 V to 7 V out at up to 2 A, with the PWM controller, both MOSFETs, a 2.2 µH shielded inductor and the control circuits sealed in one over-molded QFN. Only input and output capacitors and the feedback divider are added outside. It can also be wired as an inverting buck-boost to make a negative output.

A resistor divider on FB (pin 9) sets VOUT between 1 V and 7 V against a 1 V reference. The upper resistor RFBT is 10 kΩ; RFBB follows from the equation or the output voltage setting table, which also lists the least effective output capacitance for each voltage. Both resistors sit as close to FB as possible.
Fixed inside at 1.4 MHz and not adjustable. At heavier loads the module runs PWM at that frequency; as the load falls it moves into PFM and the frequency drops, cutting losses.

At least 20 µF (2 × 10 µF) of X5R or X7R ceramic, rated above the highest input voltage. Where the load has transients, a further 47 µF of non-ceramic capacitance is recommended. If the supply is more than a few centimetres away, bulk capacitance, typically a 47 µF electrolytic, is added beside the ceramics.

The minimum is the effective capacitance in the output voltage setting table, so ceramic capacitance has to be derated for DC bias, temperature, case size, voltage rating and dielectric. Above that minimum, ceramics, low-ESR polymer types or a mix may be used, up to 1000 µF in all.

EN has precise thresholds. Above VEN-VCC-H (1 V max) the internal LDO comes up but the output stays off (standby). At VEN-H (1.23 V typ) the module begins its soft start. Falling 100 mV below VEN-H stops switching and returns to standby; below VEN-VCC-L (0.3 V min) it shuts down fully. EN may not float. It can be tied straight to VIN for self start, or driven by a logic signal; an open-drain or open-collector driver needs a pullup to a voltage above the threshold.

The internal UVLO starts the module at 3.55 V typical on VIN and stops it about 500 mV lower (3.05 V typ). A divider from VIN to EN to AGND sets a higher start voltage, using the 1.23 V EN threshold and its 100 mV hysteresis. Setting this threshold near 80% to 85% of the lowest expected input voltage is recommended for clean start-up and smaller input surges.

PGOOD is an open-drain flag needing a pullup, typically 10 kΩ to 100 kΩ, to 18 V or less; V5V may be that supply. Sink current should stay at 3 mA or below. The flag goes high once the output climbs past 94% of its set value, and pulls low if the output drops under 92% or climbs over 107% (it releases again on falling back to 105%).

At light load the high-side MOSFET stays on until the inductor current reaches about 1 A. With little headroom between VIN and VOUT this takes longer, extra energy reaches the output and the ripple grows. Keeping at least 1 V of headroom with the EN UVLO, or adding output capacitance, avoids it.

To hold regulation over temperature, VIN should be at least 3.8 V or VOUT + 1 V, whichever is larger. With less headroom the module lowers its switching frequency (frequency foldback) to keep regulating as the input sinks. Higher ambient temperature moves dropout and foldback to a higher input voltage. The dropout and foldback curves are at 25 °C.

Overloads are limited cycle by cycle; the threshold is 3.5 A typical and shifts a little with input and output voltage. A persisting fault or short (FB below 0.4 V) puts the module into hiccup: it shuts off, waits 94 ms typical, then retries, over and over until the fault clears, after which it restarts with a normal soft start.
Switching stops when the junction passes about 165 °C and the power-up sequence starts again once it has cooled below about 148 °C.
Start-up ramps the output over an internal 4 ms soft start, and the module can start into an output that already holds a voltage (pre-biased).

The module moves between PFM at light load and PWM at heavier load; the load current of the change depends on VIN and VOUT (the PFM/PWM threshold curves; above a curve it is in PWM). Where a threshold curve is solid the PWM frequency is the nominal 1.4 MHz; on its dashed stretch (the 1 V and 1.8 V curves above about 15 V input) the PWM frequency is reduced by the controller’s minimum on-time. In PWM the duty cycle is modulated at fixed frequency, giving tight line and load regulation and low ripple. In PFM the high-side switch fires in bursts of one or more pulses whose rate regulates the output, with diode emulation, giving high light-load efficiency at the cost of larger ripple and a varying frequency. Where the frequency matters, the mode at each condition should be checked by test.
Active when VIN is above its turn-on threshold and EN is above its high threshold. With EN below its low threshold the module is shut down and draws 5 µA typical.

The supply should be well regulated over 3.8 V to 36 V, deliver the full input current, and have low enough resistance that an input current step does not pull VIN down far enough to trip a false UVLO.

Wide copper areas for VIN, VOUT and PGND to lower conduction loss and heating. Ceramic input and output capacitors right at the pins; any further output capacitors between those ceramics and the load. AGND to PGND at one point. RFBT and RFBB close to FB. Several vias from each power plane to inner layers. The thermal pad is soldered to the board; vias in it are optional and, if used, filled, plugged or tented.

RθJA falls with board copper area: from about 23 °C/W at 30 cm² to about 19 °C/W at 80 cm² on a 4-layer board. Take the highest dissipation from the power dissipation curves, work out the allowed RθJA with the equation, then read the least board area from the curve. The safe operating area curves give the highest ambient against load on an 85 mm × 65 mm, 4-layer, 2-oz. board.

Radiated emissions meet EN55011 (CISPR 11) Class B. Typical plots, 30 MHz to 1 GHz against the CISPR Class A and Class B 10 m limits, were taken on the evaluation module with no input filter, antenna horizontal and vertical, at 24 V and at 12 V in, 5 V out, 2 A.
MSL 3 with a 245 °C peak reflow, at most three reflows. Shock and vibration tested to Mil-STD-883D.
